entities.title: Native-first examples
entities.summary: What chrono, chrono-tz, std and serde_json do for each everyday task, as unit tests organized by the native type and function, each compared with UTV.
entities.purpose: Covers every scenario of docs/example-tests.md that the native side can express at all, from that side: one file per native type (naive_date, date_time, tz, system_time, json, ...) and one inner module per function (naive_date::checked_add_months::clamps_to_the_last_day_when_the_day_is_missing_from_the_target_month). Where the two agree, the expected value is computed with UTV; where they differ it is a literal, and the doc comment says what UTV does instead.
boundaries: One integration-test target, built from main.rs.
std has no calendar types, so "native" is chrono with chrono-tz, plus std::time::SystemTime, std::ops ranges and serde_json.
The zone tests use the tz database compiled into chrono-tz (release 2025b in chrono-tz 0.10.4), not the host's; UTV uses the pinned demo rules through tests/fixtures.
The three now tests (local, utc, system_time) read the real clock, and local also this machine's zone, on purpose; their doc comments say why the outcome cannot depend on it.
